target.title: fix(cron): validate failureAlert channel at the gateway boundary
target.body:
Closes #103864

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a cron failure alert would have the alert silently never delivered when they passed a channel id to `--failure-alert-channel`. That flag names a channel **type** (`last|slack|telegram|...`), but Slack labels an id like `C0EXAMPLE01` a "channel ID", so it is natural to pass it there. The value was stored unvalidated and only failed later at delivery time with `OutboundDeliveryError: channel_not_found`, with no hint about the real mistake.

The sibling `--channel` (delivery) path is already validated server-side (added for #67602). This gap is specifically the separate `failureAlert` field, which nothing validated.

## Why This Change Was Made

`--failure-alert-channel` writes `patch.failureAlert.channel`, a distinct field from `delivery` with its own store columns (`failure-alert-codec.ts`) and its own delivery path (`src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts`). The gateway validator `assertValidCronUpdatePatch` only ran channel checks `if ("delivery" in params.patch)`, so a failure-alert-only patch skipped validation and `context.cron.update` was called with the invalid channel.

`assertValidCronFailureAlert` (in `src/cron/delivery-channel-validation.ts`) reuses the existing announce-channel validation, wired into `assertValidCronCreateDelivery` and `assertValidCronUpdatePatch`. It mirrors `resolveFailureAlert()` runtime resolution exactly so it neither over- nor under-rejects:

- **Mode inheritance:** an alert that omits `mode` inherits the global cron failure-alert mode (`cfg.cron.failureAlert.mode`); webhook-mode alerts POST to `to`, so their channel type is not validated.
- **Channel/target inheritance:** an alert that omits its own channel/target inherits the job delivery channel and `to`; the final channel is resolved from that effective pair (a provider prefix in `to` wins only when the effective channel is unset/`last`). This inherits even when the alert names no route of its own, so a routing-changing edit that activates a legacy-invalid inherited delivery channel is rejected up front rather than only when the alert fires. A bare target with no resolvable channel is still rejected as ambiguous in multi-channel configs, and a `channel: null` clear that falls back to `last` is judged identically to the delivery check.
- **Scope:** the update path validates only when the edit changes routing (the alert's own channel/target/mode, enabling a previously-off alert, or a delivery channel/`to`/`mode` change an inheriting alert depends on). Unrelated edits (`--failure-alert-after`, cooldown, and alerts already active via global config) are never blocked by a channel stored before this validation existed.
- **Error classification:** `failureAlert.channel` errors are classified as `INVALID_REQUEST` so a validation error thrown from the locked `cron.update` precondition re-check surfaces correctly, not as an internal error.

Fix stays at the gateway owner boundary; no CLI or store changes.

## User Impact

Passing an unknown channel type to `--failure-alert-channel` (or a failure alert supplied to `cron.add`/`cron.update` by any client) is now rejected immediately with a clear `INVALID_REQUEST` naming `failureAlert.channel`, instead of being stored and failing later as `channel_not_found`. Valid configured channels, inherited delivery channels, webhook-mode alerts, and unrelated edits are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Live gateway behavior (local gateway, Telegram + Slack configured)

```
# A) a Slack channel ID passed to the channel-TYPE flag is rejected before any write
$ openclaw cron edit <job> --failure-alert-channel C0EXAMPLE01
GatewayClientRequestError: invalid cron.update params: failureAlert.channel must be one of: slack, telegram

# B) a real channel TYPE is accepted and stored
$ openclaw cron edit <job> --failure-alert-channel slack
  "failureAlert": { "channel": "slack" }

# C) an unrelated alert edit is not blocked (compatibility preserved)
$ openclaw cron edit <job> --failure-alert-after 3
  "failureAlert": { "after": 3 }
```

Before this change the value in (A) was stored and only failed later at delivery with `channel_not_found`.

### Regression tests (`src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts`)

Each asserts whether the gateway mutation (`context.cron.update` / `context.cron.add`) is called, so they exercise real reject-before-write behavior. Coverage includes: reject/accept explicit channel on add + update; accept correcting a stale channel; skip unrelated edits (after) and non-routing delivery edits; inherited/global webhook mode not channel-validated; job announce mode overriding global webhook; prefixed `failureAlert.to` per configured channel; bare inherited `to` accepted / ambiguous `to` rejected; routing-changing edit activating a legacy-invalid inherited channel rejected while a valid inherited channel is accepted; enable-transition, delivery-mode, and `channel: null` `last`-fallback paths.

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  242 passed (242)
```

Also green: `cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`, `cron/store/failure-alert-codec.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:core`; `oxlint` + `oxfmt`. Rebased onto current `main`.

---

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code, reviewed and validated by me. Iterated through repeated `codex review --base origin/main` rounds until clean (mode inheritance, delivery-channel inheritance, prefixed-target resolution, enable/delivery-mode routing, and error classification were all found and fixed this way), then verified end-to-end against a live local gateway (output above).
